sharedPrompt: Create exactly ONE production-ready game avatar asset, not a concept sheet. The FIRST input image is this character's original pixel sprite: preserve its identity, main colors and distinctive costume motifs. The SECOND input image is the user's APPROVED Minecraft style direction: borrow ONLY its polished block-model rendering, pixel texture shading and cute readable face, not its costume or black/purple colors. Output a single full-body character on a genuinely transparent alpha background. Minecraft character geometry: cubic head, rectangular cuboid torso, straight blocky arms and legs, crisp low-resolution pixel textures, flat voxel surfaces, no rounded anime anatomy. Camera is almost front-on with a very subtle three-quarter view (about 10 degrees), head looking straight at viewer, feet aligned, arms resting straight down slightly apart from torso. Head and boots completely visible, centered upright figure, tight but safe 5% transparent margins, no ground plane, no cast shadow, no pedestal, no background particles, no props, no duplicate views, no inset portrait, no text or watermark. Match standard Minecraft player proportions: head 8 units, torso 12 units, legs 12 units, arms 4 units wide; keep hair/clothing angular, face readable as a small icon. Detailed but coherent pixel shading with crisp blocky highlights, no watercolor, no painting, no realistic skin. Friendly approachable game character, suitable for a child's arithmetic app. Preserve the outfit's unique color palette instead of recoloring every character alike. Character-specific design:  Use a clean hard-edged cutout silhouette: absolutely NO halo, bloom, glow, soft surrounding aura or smoky feathering; outside the character must be fully transparent.  Lighting: soft even ambient illumination on the character surfaces ONLY. No backlight, no rim-light, no fog, no vignette. Clean asset extraction is essential.
